title: Scalar adjunction transport between internal and sectionwise module sheaves
statement:
Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe, with abelian sheafification whose local equivalences are monoidal, and its closed symmetric monoidal sheaf tensor [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. For a commutative ring object $R$ let $R_{\rm sec}$ be its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and let $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\rm sec})$ be the equivalence preserving underlying sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Given a ring-object map $a:R\to S$, write $a_{\rm sec}:R_{\rm sec}\to S_{\rm sec}$ for its section map. Internal restriction and coequalizer extension are those of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; sectionwise restriction and sheafified extension use [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then there are canonical natural identifications
$$E_R\operatorname{Res}_a\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_S,\qquad E_S\operatorname{Ext}_a\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_R,$$
with the latter sending the balanced generator $s\otimes m$ to the same generator. They identify the specified extension/restriction adjunctions, including unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and counit $s\otimes n\mapsto sn$.

On ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] their termwise equivalences identify the K-flat derived scalar extensions [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and exact derived restrictions, including these specified derived adjunctions. On flat-term K-flat representatives the extension comparison is the localization of the displayed termwise map. There is no flatness assumption on $a$.

proof.text: Construct the section ScalarDerivedPair using the existing prescribed sheafified extension and universal derived pair, together with sheafRingDerivedCoefficientAdjunction. Its ordinary unit is sheafification of 1 tensor m, and its K-flat transpose normalization gives the required ScalarDerivedPair normalization. The homotopy/complex quotient comparisons have identity components.

Internal restriction followed by section reconstruction is naturally isomorphic to section restriction followed by reconstruction. Its components and inverses are identity functions on sections. Their linearity is precisely naturality of the lax tensorator of the sheaf inclusion with respect to a.

Take the inverse mate of this restriction square under the two ordinary scalar adjunctions. A mate of an isomorphism along equivalences is invertible (apply the mate-isomorphism theorem to opposite adjunctions). Its inverse is the extension comparison. The mate-unit identity implies the ordinary Hom transpose identity by naturality.

The internal coequalizer identity S tensor extendUnitHom followed by the extension action equals extendπ shows that the balanced generator s tensor m equals s times the ordinary internal unit at m. The mate-unit identity identifies its image with s times the section ordinary unit. S-linearity of extension comparison, eqToHom, and module sheafification then gives the same sectionwise pure tensor s tensor m. No general balanced-bilinear universal-property theorem is needed.

Apply lem-sfb-derived-section-scalar-transport to the ordinary restriction and extension squares and the proved Hom transpose identity. It supplies the universal internal derived pair, computation on sectionwise K-flat complexes, normalized internal unit, canonical localized restriction square, representative extension square and all derived Hom transpose identities. Combine these data with the identity restriction components and balanced-generator calculation.
